hints: Define $f(x) = \mathrm{e}^{2x} - 5 - \cos(3x)$ and evaluate at $x = 0.7$ and $x = 0.8$ in radian mode.
Demonstrate a sign change between $f(0.7)$ and $f(0.8)$ to confirm the presence of the root.
walkthrough: Define the continuous function $f(x) = \mathrm{e}^{2x} - 5 - \cos(3x)$ for $x \in [0.7, 0.8]$ in radians.

Conclude by the intermediate value theorem:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous on $[0.7, 0.8]$ and $f(0.7) < 0$ while $f(0.8) > 0$, there is a sign change. Therefore, the equation has a root in the interval $0.7 < x < 0.8$.

Since this is identical to the equation in part (a), the sequence converges to the root of that equation.
